title: Lesson Plan — Power-sharing (Class 10 CBSE Civics)
subject: Social Science (Civics)
objectives: Describe the ethnic composition and political tensions in Belgium and Sri Lanka.
Explain why majoritarianism led to civil war in Sri Lanka.
Identify the key features of Belgium's power-sharing model.
Explain the prudential and moral reasons for power-sharing.
Compare horizontal and vertical distributions of power.
Identify forms of power-sharing among social groups and political parties.
prerequisites: Familiarity with democracy as 'rule by the people' from Class 9.
Knowledge of India's Constitution and three-tier government from earlier classes.
materials: Map of Belgium with linguistic regions
Map of Sri Lanka with ethnic distribution
A timeline strip of Sri Lanka 1948 → 2009

activities.description: Hook: 'A class of 50 — 40 students want extra lunch, 10 don't. Should the 40 simply impose their wish? Why or why not?' Take views; introduce the idea that democracy needs more than majority count.
Two case studies (Belgium and Sri Lanka). Students read short summaries and fill a comparison table: ethnic groups, government policy, outcome.
Cover four blocks: (i) Belgium and Sri Lanka in detail; (ii) majoritarianism vs accommodation; (iii) prudential and moral reasons; (iv) four forms of power-sharing with Indian and global examples.
teacher_actions: Sketch a Belgian-government diagram on the board (centre + 2 state govts + Brussels + community govts).
Drill the dates of Sri Lankan majoritarianism.
List four forms of power-sharing with examples.
student_actions: Match Indian examples to each form.

activities.description: Worksheet practice: 6 questions covering definitions, comparisons and a short-answer on Belgium vs Sri Lanka.
Exit ticket: 4 questions, one from each block.
Homework: list 3 examples of power-sharing in your daily life (school council, family, sports team) and classify each as horizontal, vertical or social-group.

homework: Make a comparison table of Belgium and Sri Lanka — population, language groups, government approach, outcome.
List 3 examples of power-sharing in your school or community; classify each.
Read the news for one day and find one example of horizontal, vertical, social-group or party power-sharing in India.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Run a 10-question quiz next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on Belgium vs Sri Lanka with a 5-point rubric.
references: NCERT Class 10 — Democratic Politics – II, Chapter 1: Power-sharing.
